mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 9.5% signals a weak labor market that may prompt the Federal Reserve to maintain accommodative monetary policy, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when UNRATE > 9.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates broad-based weakening in consumer demand, triggering a flight to safety and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not lead to negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 95 (index, 2017=100), it signals a slowing industrial sector, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST has increased for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals accelerating inflation that may lead to monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in PAYEMS and decline in UNRATE does not lead to positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of slow GDP growth (GDPC1 growth rate below 1.5% annually), economic concerns lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth rate < 1.5% annually.
